neighbours.label: the piece ' pe' (or ' summ') where the context sets up a peak: a rising trend about to 'peak' / reach its high point
fire: Membership grew quickly through the decade, peaking at nearly two million in 1975.
Ticket sales rose all through the summer, peaking in August with sold-out shows.
Rainfall increased steadily from March onward, peaking in late July.
The price of copper climbed for three years, peaking at a record high in 2011.
Her popularity grew with every album, peaking with the release of her third record.
Website traffic rose sharply after the launch, peaking on the second day.
The river kept rising overnight, peaking just below the top of the levee.
Enrollment expanded each year after the reform, peaking at 900 students in 2019.
quiet: Membership shrank quickly through the decade, falling to just two hundred in 1975.
Ticket sales stayed flat all through the summer, with half-empty halls in August.
The boy skipped a flat pebble across the pond and counted the bounces.
The price of copper fell for three years, hitting a record low in 2011.
The doctor ordered an X-ray of her pelvis after the fall on the ice.
Website traffic dropped sharply after the outage, recovering only a week later.
The river kept falling overnight, exposing the rocks along the bank.
Enrollment declined each year after the reform, dropping to 300 students in 2019.

predictions: 8/8 fire on ' pe' of 'peaking' after a rise; near misses with 'pebble'/'pelvis' or a trend that bottoms out stay quiet
